samples.summary: Peer-controlled `listLevel` is still unvalidated at the CRDT read boundary; the new normalization only fires when a local indent gesture happens to touch the block, while layout/paint/export keep reading the raw value
samples.evidence: `treeNodeToBlock` writes `block.listLevel = Number(attrs.listLevel)` (packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:243) with no finiteness or range check, so any collaborator with write access to the shared Yorkie tree (or a crafted/replayed change) can set the attribute to `"1e12"`, `"-1"` or `"abc"`. That value flows raw into geometry on every *other* consumer: `layout.ts:494` (`LIST_INDENT_PX * ((block.listLevel ?? 0) + 1)` added to `marginLeft`), `table-layout.ts:93`, `paint-layout.ts:198`, `doc-canvas.ts:599`, `table-renderer.ts:524`, `peer-cursor.ts:392` and the PDF exporter `pdf-painter.ts:366/589`. Result for every *viewer* of the document (including read-only share links, where no write path is involved at all): NaN/absurd marginLeft, collapsed or garbage line-breaking geometry, and a broken or hung render/export — a remotely triggered client-side DoS, not just a local glitch. The change under review introduces `levelOf()` (packages/docs/src/model/list-level.ts:29-33), whose doc comment asserts "Normalizing at the single point of read is what keeps both guards total" — but the planner is not the point of read; it only repairs a block that a local indent/outdent gesture happens to cover, so the sanitizer reads as covering the vector while the actual ingest boundary stays open. Clamping in `treeNodeToBlock` (as `clipboard.ts:348-351` already does for the paste boundary, now with the shared `MAX_LIST_LEVEL`) is what would close it. Confidence is medium because I traced the untrusted value into the geometry multiplications but did not confirm a hard hang/crash in the line-breaker with a NaN width.

samples.summary: Write amplification: a single Tab/Cmd+] keystroke now writes every block of an attacker-shaped list run, and each write re-reads+deep-clones the whole document — one keypress becomes O(N²) work
samples.evidence: Before this change a level gesture wrote only the blocks the selection covered (bounded by what the user selected). Now `planSiblingGroup` (packages/docs/src/model/list-level.ts:96-104) emits a change for every block in the derived subtree, and `applyListLevelChanges` issues one `doc.setBlockType` per change (view/text-editor.ts:2727-2732, view/editor.ts:1607-1612, view/text-box-editor.ts:830-835). `Doc.setBlockType` calls `refresh()` and possibly a second `refresh()` (model/document.ts:662-667), and `YorkieDocStore.getDocument()` deep-clones the entire document on every read (`cloneDocument` = `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(doc))`, packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:527-632). A collaborator who plants a long run of items at levels `0,1,1,1,…` (or a crafted `WAFFLEDOCS_MIME` paste payload, which `sanitizeBlock` happily accepts with clamped levels) turns one Tab on the run's head into N full-document rebuilds inside a single `doc.update`, i.e. quadratic time/allocation and a frozen tab. The subtree scan itself is linear (subtrees are disjoint), so the cost is entirely in the per-write refresh; a bulk/batched write or a single refresh at the end of the batch would remove the amplification.

samples.summary: `TextEditor.siblingsOf` resolves a stale layout cell-parent through throwing `getBlock`, so a table deleted by a remote peer turns the next Tab into an uncaught exception mid-gesture — the twin in editor.ts deliberately uses `findBlock`
samples.evidence: `siblingsOf` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2886-2896) takes `info` from `getCellInfo`, which reads `getActiveLayout().blockParentMap` (text-editor.ts:3666-3671) — a map only as fresh as the last layout pass — and then calls `this.doc.getBlock(info.tableBlockId)`, which throws `Block not found` (model/document.ts:202-216). A collaborator deleting the table between the last layout and the local keystroke makes Tab / Cmd+] throw out of the keydown handler, aborting the gesture (and, under `Doc.batch`, discarding the Yorkie clone). The `siblingsOf` added in the same change in `view/editor.ts:1638-1648` uses `doc.findBlock` for exactly this stated reason, so the two copies disagree; the throwing one is the newly added code path for the cursor-only case. Impact is a remote-triggered client-side error rather than data exposure, hence minor; confidence low because the stale window depends on layout invalidation timing I did not fully trace, and a similar pre-existing `getBlock` sits at text-editor.ts:2835.

verdict.reason: The absence claim is factually correct — I confirmed `treeNodeToBlock` writes `block.listLevel = Number(attrs.listLevel)` with no clamp (packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:243), and the live editor's twin reader is identical (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:494-496); only clipboard.ts:348-351 and list-level.ts:29-33 normalize. But it is not blocking under the Security rubric. (a) No trust boundary is crossed: the attribute can only be set by a party who already holds write access to the shared tree, and that same actor can already replace all content; `listLevel` is not a permission gate, secret, injection sink or crypto check, and it sits beside a dozen equally unvalidated `Number(...)` reads in the same function (fontSize :70, padding :129, colSpan/rowSpan :168-169). (b) The claimed DoS does not materialize: I traced the line-breaker at layout.ts:753-793 — with NaN every comparison is false (no wrap, clean exit), and with a hugely negative effectiveWidth the char fallback still advances (`endIdx > charIdx + 1` breaks the inner while; flushLine() empties currentRuns so the `continue` at :776 cannot loop), so output is bounded by text length, no hang or unbounded allocation. (c) No server-side exposure: the backend's only consumer readDocsRoot (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:239-257) is reached from api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:129 which returns JSON and never lays out or paints; the one allocation-sensitive site, `'  '.repeat(...)` in serialize/markdown.ts:140, is invoked only from the client-side CLI (packages/cli/src/docs/content.ts:129). What remains is a rendering-robustness/correctness defect for the correctness lens, not an authz/secrets/injection/crypto/SSRF/deserialization issue.

finding.summary: Peer-supplied `listLevel` is still read through a bare `Number(...)` with no clamp; the new `levelOf()` normalizer only protects the planner, so a poisoned level keeps reaching raw sinks (unbounded `String.repeat` in the markdown serializer, NaN/huge geometry in layout and PDF)
finding.evidence: The new module documents the threat itself (`packages/docs/src/model/list-level.ts:19-27`: "a peer's Tree attribute is read straight through `Number(...)`") and claims "Normalizing at the single point of read is what keeps both guards total". That is only true inside `planListLevelChanges`. The actual read boundaries are unchanged and unclamped: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:495` (`block.listLevel = Number(attrs.listLevel)`) and `packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:243` (same line, used for revision previews). Attack: a principal with write access to a shared doc (collaborator, or an API key with write scope via `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/:w/documents/:d/content`, which does not validate `listLevel` — see the companion finding) stores `listLevel: 1e9` (or `1e400` → `"Infinity"`). Every other reader then deserializes it verbatim. Sinks reached with the raw value: `packages/docs/src/serialize/markdown.ts:140` `'  '.repeat(Math.max(0, block.listLevel ?? 0))` → 2e9-char allocation or `RangeError: Invalid string length`, crashing `wafflebase docs content get --format md` (`packages/cli/src/docs/content.ts:129`) for anyone who exports the document; `packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:494` `LIST_INDENT_PX * ((block.listLevel ?? 0) + 1)` → NaN/Infinity `marginLeft` that collapses or blanks the rendered document; `packages/docs/src/export/pdf-painter.ts:377` → NaN/huge coordinates into pdf-lib. Note the adjacent `headingLevel` is clamped at its sink (`markdown.ts:156 clampHeadingLevel`) while `listLevel` is not. This is a persistent, other-user-affecting availability/data-integrity issue, not merely a local render glitch.

verdict.reason: All claimed code exists as described. `levelOf()` in packages/docs/src/model/list-level.ts:29-33 is private to the planner (not exported; used only by subtreeOf/planSiblingGroup), while the actual deserialization boundaries remain unclamped: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:495 and packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:243 both do a bare `Number(attrs.listLevel)`. The raw value reaches unbounded sinks: markdown.ts:140 `'  '.repeat(Math.max(0, block.listLevel ?? 0))` (unbounded allocation / RangeError), layout.ts:494 `LIST_INDENT_PX * ((block.listLevel ?? 0) + 1)` folded into marginLeft, and pdf-painter.ts:366/589. The asymmetry is real: headingLevel is clamped at its sink (markdown.ts:132 via clampHeadingLevel at :156-160), listLevel is not, and the only clamps in the tree are clipboard.ts:351 (paste) and list-level.ts:32 (planner). The persistence vector is reachable: docs-content.controller.ts:429-443 assertValidBlock validates id/type/style/tableData but never listLevel, and docs-tree.ts:178 writes `String(block.listLevel)` verbatim, so a collaborator or write-scoped API key can store a poisoned level that every other reader deserializes, crashing `docs content get --format md` (cli/src/docs/content.ts:128-129) and corrupting layout/PDF geometry for other users. No guard elsewhere makes this unreachable; unvalidated cross-principal input flowing into unbounded allocation is unsafe input handling within the security lane.

finding.summary: The docs content PUT validator checks every block-style numeric is finite but never validates `listLevel`, so the API is an unvalidated injection point for the out-of-range/non-finite list levels the new planner's normalizer exists to defend against
finding.evidence: `assertValidBlock` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:429-511) validates `id`, `type`, `style` shape, `style.alignment` against an allowlist and every `BLOCK_STYLE_NUMERIC_FIELDS` entry as a finite number (:399-407), and `assertValidHeaderFooter` even validates `marginFromEdge` as finite (:331-339) — but nothing checks `listLevel`. `buildBlockNode` then persists it verbatim: `packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:178` `attrs.listLevel = String(block.listLevel)`. So `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/:w/documents/:d/content` with `{blocks:[{id:"a",type:"list-item",listLevel:1e9,inlines:[],style:{}}]}` is accepted by an authenticated write-scoped caller and lands in the CRDT for every collaborator, where the readers cited in the companion finding consume it raw (`'  '.repeat(1e9)` in the markdown serializer → RangeError/GB allocation; NaN geometry in layout). The clamp exists in exactly two places today — the clipboard parser and the new `levelOf` in `model/list-level.ts:29-33` — and neither is on this path. `MAX_LIST_LEVEL` is now an exported model constant, so the same bound is trivially applicable here (`@wafflebase/docs` is already imported by this controller at :44-49).

verdict.reason: The factual absence is real: assertValidBlock / assertValidBlockStyle (docs-content.controller.ts:429-511, :380-427) never check listLevel, and a repo-wide grep shows the backend's only use is verbatim persistence at yorkie/docs-tree.ts:178 - no clamp, and MAX_LIST_LEVEL (packages/docs/src/model/list-level.ts:7) is not imported by the backend. It is nonetheless out of this lens's lane and non-blocking. (1) The endpoint is reachable only by an authenticated workspace member or a workspace-bound API key holding the write scope (controller :90; workspace-scope.guard.ts:40-45; api-key-write-scope.guard.ts:42-48), i.e. an actor already entitled to a destructive replace of the entire document (:160-162) - no authorization boundary is crossed and no new capability is obtained. (2) There is no interpreter sink: the value becomes a string CRDT attribute (docs-tree.ts:178); no SQL/command/path/template is involved, and no server-side consumer exists - serializeMarkdown, whose '  '.repeat() is the claimed crash primitive (packages/docs/src/serialize/markdown.ts:140), is invoked only from packages/cli/src/docs/content.ts:129 and packages/cli/src/slides/content.ts:184, never in the backend process. (3) The validator is documented as 400-vs-500 shape hygiene (:164-173) and deliberately enforces finiteness without range everywhere (marginFromEdge :331-339, BLOCK_STYLE_NUMERIC_FIELDS :399-407), so the same caller already has equal-or-greater availability impact on collaborators through values that do pass validation. What remains is an input-normalization/robustness defect belonging to the correctness lens (explicitly deferred here), minor hardening at most under the security rubric - not a major security weakness.
